l4_steps.name: Retrieve passenger PNR and loyalty tier status
l4_steps.input: Passenger boarding pass or loyalty card scan at lounge entry
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PNR, fare class, and loyalty tier record
l4_steps.kpi: Access verification time < 30 seconds per passenger
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa tier-lookup latency spikes during irregular operations (IRROP) can queue 20+ passengers at peak departure banks, degrading premium brand perception

l4_steps.name: Validate lounge entitlement against fare and tier
l4_steps.input: PNR, fare class code, loyalty tier from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Entitlement decision (Eligible / Not Eligible) and access tier (Standard / Premium / First)
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement accuracy rate ≥ 99.5% (no wrongful denial or admission)
l4_steps.pain_point: Misalignment between ATPCO fare class entitlement rules and Comarch loyalty tier tables causes wrongful denials for premium codeshare passengers not in airline's own PSS

l4_steps.name: Check real-time lounge occupancy vs. capacity cap
l4_steps.input: Live occupancy count from SITA AMS badge-in sensors; configured capacity limit per lounge
l4_steps.output: Current occupancy percentage; green / amber / red capacity status
l4_steps.kpi: Lounge occupancy maintained at ≤ 90% of rated capacity during peak banks
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS occupancy sensors in third-party contract lounges (e.g. airport operator lounges) are not integrated, requiring manual headcounts and creating data lag of 5–10 minutes

l4_steps.name: Issue digital lounge access pass or redirect passenger
l4_steps.input: Entitlement decision from 1.2; occupancy status from 1.3
l4_steps.output: Digital lounge pass (QR code) issued to eligible passenger, or voucher / priority queue token issued when capacity exceeded
l4_steps.kpi: Guest satisfaction with access process ≥ 4.2 / 5.0 (post-visit survey)
l4_steps.pain_point: No dynamic overbooking buffer in Altéa lounge module — capacity denial is binary, leading to complaints when eligible passengers are turned away 1–2 seats below hard cap

l4_steps.name: Forecast lounge demand from departure schedule
l4_steps.input: Published schedule SSIM file; historical lounge utilisation by departure bank; loyalty tier passenger mix from Comarch
l4_steps.output: Hourly demand forecast per lounge (expected arrivals by tier) for next 72 hours
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy within ± 10% of actual peak occupancy
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS schedule feed does not include real-time irregular-operations (IRROP) rebooking data; demand spikes from cancelled flight consolidations are not reflected until T-4 hours

l4_steps.name: Generate staffing and F&B resource plan
l4_steps.input: 72-hour demand forecast from 2.1; staffing contracts and F&B par levels
l4_steps.output: Shift roster, F&B order quantities, amenity replenishment schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Staff-to-guest ratio ≥ 1:15 during peak departure banks; F&B stockout rate < 1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Resource planning is manual in spreadsheets at most stations — no integrated workforce management system feeding lounge-specific demand signals, leading to over/understaffing 30% of departure banks

l4_steps.name: Submit F&B and consumables requisition to catering
l4_steps.input: F&B order quantities from 2.2; approved supplier catalogue
l4_steps.output: Purchase orders raised in SAP Ariba; delivery confirmed for T-3 hours pre-departure bank
l4_steps.kpi: Catering order fulfilment rate ≥ 98% within agreed lead time
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba supplier catalogue is managed by central procurement and updated quarterly — lounge-specific seasonal menu changes or regional items cannot be added ad hoc, limiting localisation of premium experience

l4_steps.name: Activate surge staffing protocol for high-load windows
l4_steps.input: Forecast showing > 80% occupancy in any 30-minute window; SITA AMS flight load alerts
l4_steps.output: Surge staffing confirmation; overflow lounge section opened (if available); partner lounge access tokens issued
l4_steps.kpi: Surge activation lead time ≤ 2 hours before predicted peak; guest wait time at entry ≤ 5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Overflow agreements with airport operator lounges are station-specific and not codified in SITA AMS — activation requires manual phone calls, causing delays of 20–30 minutes in agreeing capacity at short notice

l4_steps.name: Retrieve passenger profile and service preferences
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR and loyalty ID from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Passenger profile: dietary preferences, language, past complaints, upgrade history, service notes
l4_steps.kpi: Profile retrieval at lounge entry < 15 seconds; preference recognition rate ≥ 85% of repeat premium guests
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce CRM preference data is updated via post-flight survey only — real-time in-flight service notes from cabin crew (e.g., passenger declined meal) are not written back to CRM, causing repeat service failures on next journey

l4_steps.name: Flag VIP, VVIP, and special service requests on manifest
l4_steps.input: Day-of-operations manifest; CRM profile flags from 3.1; SSR codes (VVIP, WCHR, MEDA, SPML)
l4_steps.output: Annotated manifest with VIP tier flags, SSR types, and assigned concierge owner per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SSR-flagged premium passengers identified ≥ 90 minutes prior to departure
l4_steps.pain_point: VVIP flags set by sales or government affairs teams are stored in a separate SharePoint list not integrated with Altéa PSS — lounge staff miss VVIPs when SharePoint is not checked manually before each departure bank

l4_steps.name: Coordinate personalised amenity kits and premium meal setup
l4_steps.input: Annotated manifest from 3.2; dietary and preference data from Salesforce CRM; catering delivery confirmation from 2.3
l4_steps.output: Personalised amenity kit assignment per seat; meal pre-selection recorded in catering order
l4_steps.kpi: Meal pre-selection accuracy ≥ 97%; amenity kit shortfall rate < 0.5% of premium seats
l4_steps.pain_point: Pre-selection data from Salesforce CRM must be manually transcribed into the catering system — no API integration between CRM preference data and catering management platform increases transcription error rate to ~3%

l4_steps.name: Activate meet-and-greet and dedicated butler for VIPs
l4_steps.input: VIP / VVIP flag from step 3.2; expected arrival time from SITA AMS inbound flight status
l4_steps.output: Named concierge assigned to VIP; curbside or airside meet-and-greet schedule confirmed; butler service briefing completed
l4_steps.kpi: VIP meet-and-greet execution rate 100% of flagged passengers; greeting delay < 5 minutes from arrival
l4_steps.pain_point: Inbound flight delays not surfaced in Salesforce CRM require concierge to monitor SITA AMS separately — no unified notification when VIP inbound flight is delayed > 30 minutes, leading to missed or premature meet-and-greets

l4_steps.name: Execute lounge F&B, spa, and digital amenity service
l4_steps.input: Active guest list from SITA AMS lounge occupancy module; F&B stock confirmed in 2.3
l4_steps.output: Service log per guest (items consumed, special requests fulfilled, service timestamps)
l4_steps.kpi: F&B replenishment cycle ≤ 20 minutes; spa booking wait time ≤ 10 minutes; Wi-Fi uptime ≥ 99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Service logging is paper-based in most third-party contract lounges — consumption data is not captured digitally, preventing demand pattern analysis and cost reconciliation accuracy, leading to billing disputes with caterers

l4_steps.name: Broadcast boarding gate notifications to lounge guests
l4_steps.input: Gate departure T-30 and T-15 alerts from SITA AMS flight information display system (FIDS)
l4_steps.output: Visual and audio boarding alerts in lounge; individual SMS / app push notifications to guests
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding notification issued ≥ 30 minutes before STD; missed notification rate < 0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS FIDS integration is reliable at hub stations but frequently lags at outstations (> 5 minutes) — lounge staff rely on personal phone calls to gate agents for departure time confirmation at 30% of stations

l4_steps.name: Escalate and resolve in-lounge SSR requests
l4_steps.input: Guest SSR codes from step 3.2; real-time service requests raised at lounge reception
l4_steps.output: SSR resolved or escalated to operations; record updated in Altéa PSS with resolution notes
l4_steps.kpi: SSR resolution within lounge: ≥ 90% within 15 minutes; escalation to operations < 5% of SSRs
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS SSR update requires back-office terminal access — lounge concierges using mobile devices cannot update SSR records in real time, causing duplication of effort when the same request is re-raised at the gate

l4_steps.name: Execute no-show baggage offload for gate-close no-shows
l4_steps.input: Final boarding close signal from SITA AMS; passenger no-show confirmation from gate agent
l4_steps.output: Offload order issued in Altéa PSS; baggage reconciliation request sent to ramp; lounge access record closed
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage offload completion within 15 minutes of gate close; no-show offload accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lounge no-show visibility depends on gate agent manually communicating non-boarding to the lounge — no automated Altéa trigger when a premium passenger clears lounge entry but does not scan boarding pass at gate, causing offload delays that breach 15-minute target

l4_steps.name: Capture post-lounge NPS and satisfaction scores
l4_steps.input: Lounge visit closed (guest departed for gate); guest contact details from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: NPS score per visit; free-text feedback categorised by theme (F&B, Staff, Comfort, Connectivity)
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥ 35% of lounge visitors; Lounge NPS target ≥ 75
l4_steps.pain_point: Medallia survey invitation is triggered by flight departure, not lounge exit — passengers in transit or connecting through a second lounge receive duplicate invitations, inflating response counts and skewing NPS by station

l4_steps.name: Review KPI dashboard and trigger service recovery if below threshold
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, occupancy data, F&B stockout events, SSR resolution rates from Medallia and SITA AMS
l4_steps.output: Weekly KPI report; service recovery action plan if NPS < 75 or complaint rate > 2%; trend analysis by station
l4_steps.kpi: KPI dashboard refresh latency ≤ 24 hours; corrective action plans issued within 48 hours of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from multiple source systems (Medallia, SITA AMS, Altéa, SAP Ariba) with inconsistent refresh cadences — data as-of timestamps differ by up to 48 hours, making same-week service recovery decisions unreliable for fast-moving operational issues
